title: Shared compression library: a NUMA boot warning stopped validation
subtitle: codex (gpt-6) · line: xswap-compression-tiering · base 5e84ca92 · 1 candidate · 3 guests / 0 builds

verdict.headline: Baseline and debug runs passed; a NUMA boot warning kept correctness incomplete.

tiles.label: Baseline and debug
tiles.note: Complete gates for those two runs.

sections.title: One hypothesis across retained infrastructure contracts
sections.lead: R3 tested the same shared compression library. Fresh baseline and candidate debug runs passed their per-run gates. The two-node NUMA guest failed on a genuine boot warning, closing this infrastructure contract.

blocks.text: The unchanged kernel reached validated debug coverage. The full required matrix remains incomplete, so calibration, performance and dependent architecture phases remain pending.
R3 used 3 probe guests and no new builds; existing builds were revalidated and reused. Through this closeout, original C1 plus R2 and R3 consumed 8 guests and 4 builds.

sections.title: 1. Whole system: restore the application page
sections.lead: An application needs its full page in physical RAM. Stored contents may be compressed inside RAM or reside on a backing device. Compression trades CPU work for less storage traffic.

blocks.takeaway: The changed engine serves compressed contents inside RAM
blocks.note: Schematic path, with no illustrative size or timing used as a measurement.

blocks.text: The candidate changes the compressed-storage implementation. The existing frontend still decides admission, accounting and writeback. No new RAM-to-disk migration policy is implemented here.

sections.title: 2. Subsystem: policy keeps the object identity
sections.lead: ZSwap retains the entry index, memory-group charge, ordering and lifetime pins. A shared page library owns per-CPU codec contexts, scratch buffers and compressed-object storage.

blocks.takeaway: Data moves through the engine; policy stays with the frontend

blocks.text: High-confidence source review supports this ownership boundary. CPU-local codec contexts and requested memory placement require runtime coverage. The single-node debug case passed; the NUMA warning preserves an unresolved validation boundary.

sections.title: 3. Concrete test: split memory nodes exposed a boot warning
sections.lead: The same candidate image passed its single-node debug case. The auxiliary NUMA guest split four virtual CPUs across two memory nodes while retaining an implicit package topology.

blocks.takeaway: Single-node debug: the complete per-run check passed
NUMA guest: a reported cache-sibling pair crossed memory nodes

blocks.text: The NUMA library, hotplug and memory-accounting subcases passed, including matching requested and actual memory nodes. The boot warning failed both kernel-warning gates, keeping the overall run failed.

High-confidence diagnosis: the virtual CPU and memory-node mapping conflict. The warning appears during CPU boot. No candidate-source defect is established by this run; complete coverage remains required.

sections.title: Review the topology correction, then gather fresh evidence
sections.lead: This frozen contract is closed with its warning intact. A separately reviewed topology correction and new remaining-budget contract must collect fresh correctness evidence before calibration.

blocks.takeaway: The next contract still has to prove its topology

blocks.text: A fresh correctly mapped topology that produces the same warning would contradict the current diagnosis. No outcome is predicted for that correction. Remaining resource ceilings and the earlier enforced deadline remain binding.
